items.text: 'Lehra do tiranga' (wave the tricolour): the CJP founder appealed to people to hoist the tricolour at Central Park, Connaught Place, at 5 pm on 16 October. He said Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to jail for hoisting the tricolour, and now it has to be shown that this is not a crime; those who cannot come to Delhi should take out tricolour marches in their own cities.

items.h: Youth Congress's 'Bring back Jantar Mantar' march sets out from Patel Chowk, police stop it near Sansad Marg police station, many workers detained
Former judge Gopala Gowda: removing Jantar Mantar from the list of protest sites is unconstitutional, a blow to the right to peaceful assembly

items.text: Rahul Gandhi held a press conference with NSUI and Youth Congress protesters. The protesters allege that during Tuesday's detention the police used sticks and kicks, and a student lost the hearing in one ear. Rahul promised action. Delhi Police has not yet replied.

The other side: American singer Mary Millben claims that CJP gets money from anti-Modi 'donors' in the US, and she asked Indian youth to stand up against it. No evidence was put forward for the claim.

Saurav Das was kept in Jail No. 2 at Tihar and Ashutosh Ranka in Jail No. 4. Bail applications for both are being filed in Patiala House Court. Two FIRs have been filed in the case, at the Connaught Place and Parliament Street police stations.

Trinamool MP Mahua Moitra shared the video of the CJP leaders climbing the gate into Jantar Mantar and said this cannot be a crime, and if the Supreme Court stays silent it will be seen as a partner in the murder of the Constitution.
DMK chief M.K. Stalin warned that if more young people are sent to jail, more ordinary people will join the movement. He said the DMK will give legal help to Ranka and Das.
AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal asked about the arrests: is waving your own flag in your own country a crime?

items.h: Rahul Gandhi: sending young people to jail for waving the tricolour is cowardice; Jantar Mantar belongs to the people, and we will take it back

items.text: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said in Nagpur that the fight of CJP and the INDIA alliance is one, but CJP is an independent pressure group fighting against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He said he does not need security.

items.h: Abhijeet Dipke asks: what was the crime of Saurav and Ranka, hoisting the tricolour at Jantar Mantar?

items.text: The Special Executive Magistrate's court sent CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to Tihar in five days' judicial custody. The third leader, Ajinkya Shinde, was released on a peace bond of Rs 5,000, on the condition that he does not disturb the peace for six months. The police's side: the two repeatedly broke Section 163 and violated the conditions of their earlier bond.

CJP's legal head Ratna Singh alleges that the three leaders were brought to Parliament Street police station in a private vehicle at 3 am and were not allowed to meet lawyers until late at night. Dipke called it a 'cowardly tactic' and said that if dissent is to be crushed, the Prime Minister should openly declare an Emergency. The police's official statement has not yet come.

Defence lawyer Abhisht Hela told the court that the police's claim that the activists had called people to Jantar Mantar was wrong, and questioned the authority of the Special Executive Magistrate who ordered the custody. According to Ajinkya Shinde, who was released, he was picked up for waving the tricolour and for the slogan 'Vande Mataram'; the party's national working committee will decide the next step.

BJP's side: Home Minister Amit Shah called Rahul Gandhi's press conference a 'manufactured media event' and an 'echo of lies'. He says that gathering workers of fourteen parties into a crowd of eight thousand over one and a half kilometres does not make anyone the voice of the country.
Rahul Gandhi: we fully respect the Chief Justice, the Supreme Court and the justice system, but political and people's resistance will continue and will win.

According to CJP, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde, who were picked up after entering Jantar Mantar on Tuesday morning, have been charged with trespass, bond violation and obstructing government work. Delhi Police called it a 'preventive arrest'.

Delhi High Court issued notice on Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib's petition against the refusal of permission to protest at Jantar Mantar; the next hearing is on 17 November. The government argued that the petition has become pointless after the denotification.
